speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe the nature of the feeding difficulties and abdominal distension, and when did these symptoms first appear? Also, how is his bowel movement pattern and stool consistency?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the baby have a fever, and have you noticed any vomiting or blood in his stool? Please also describe the color and frequency of his bowel movements.

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications. This is only for study purposes, so you do not need to list warnings or many alternatives. Please just provide the best final answer.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Abdominal X-Ray
REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Dilated bowel segments with absence of gas in the rectum, suggesting a possible obstruction

speaker: Doctor
text: The abdominal X-ray shows dilated bowel segments with an empty rectum, which strongly points to a specific motility disorder in infants. I need to confirm if the baby has ever had a meconium stool passed within the first 48 hours of life, or if there is a history of chronic constipation since birth.

speaker: Patient
text: The baby did not seem to pass stool normally and the belly swelling has become more obvious. Feeding has clearly decreased over the past few days.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did the baby pass meconium within the first 48 hours of life? I am also requesting a contrast enema to confirm the transition zone.

speaker: Patient
text: The abdomen still looks swollen and the baby seems uncomfortable, especially in the lower abdomen.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Contrast Enema
The clinical picture of delayed meconium passage, abdominal distension, and the X-ray findings are highly suggestive of Hirschsprung disease, so I am ordering a contrast enema to identify the characteristic transition zone.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: A transition zone in the distal colon, compatible with Hirschsprung disease

speaker: Doctor
text: The contrast enema results confirm the diagnosis with the characteristic transition zone. DIAGNOSIS READY: Hirschsprung disease
